newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says massacres underway by Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: France says massacres underway by Zaire rebels.

text.p: France said Tutsi-led Zairean rebels slaughtered Rwandan Hutu refugees after taking the town of Mbandaka on Tuesday, and urged an international appeal to stop the alleged massacres.
A spokesman for the Foreign Ministry said eyewitnesses in Mbandaka, northeast of Kinshasa on the Zaire river in Equator province, confirmed the killings.

"According to fully reliable sources, massacres are now being carried out in the town of Mbandaka by the APDL (Alliance of Forces for the Democratic Liberation of Congo-Zaire) forces," the Ministry said in a statement.
The spokesman some 50,000 Rwandan refugees were in the region. He could not say how many people had been killed.
"France condemns these criminal acts and voices deep indignation. It appeals to all those who can join voices in immediately demanding that human lives be respected," the ministry said.

Washington said last week there were increasingly credible reports of killings of Hutu refugees in areas held by Kabila's APDL rebels, who have seized about three-quarters of Zaire since October and are marching on Kinshasa.
United Nations and other aid agency estimate that between 200,000 and 300,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees are left in Zaire, most of them unaccounted for.
Despite promises by Kabila of free access, aid workers have still been denied access to vast parts of eastern Zaire where refugees have either fled or are feared to be dead.
Aid workers fear rebels are hunting down and killing the refugees to spare the risk, expense and trouble of repatriating them to Rwanda.
U.N. investigators and forensic experts who planned to dig up mass graves in a test of Kabila's willingness to assist human rights investigations were refused access by the Tutsi-dominated rebels.

The refugees are the rump of more than two million who fled Rwanda to Zaire and Tanzania in 1994 in fear of reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates since they fled a rebellion by Tutsi-dominated rebels in the east last year.
Some 685,000 Hutu refugees returned home from Zaire last year but the hard core trekked westwards, deeper into Zaire.
